description: Los Causas Espaciales is a project that integrates NASA satellite data, geospatial analysis, and artificial intelligence to identify and map areas exposed to climate, environmental, social, and archaeological risks. Its goal is to transform satellite data into actionable insights to anticipate risks, assess territories, and support strategic decision-making in infrastructure and sustainable development projects.
summary: TERRA 2045 · The Last Journey is a 3D web game backed by an Earth-evidence platform, built by Los Causas Espaciales for the challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!". In 2045 humanity has lost the Earth and survives on the Moon. The player travels back to 2026, lands on the real terrain of one of 57 places around the world and reads how each place has changed since 2001 using NASA data (POWER, GPM IMERG, NASADEM, MODIS, EONET). Every trend is tested with Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen and checked against a second source (ERA5, CHIRPS): when sources disagree, the game flags a "false clue" instead of hiding it. With limited resources, the player plans and warns the town before a simulated mudslide, flood, eruption or avalanche, and every place kept safe heals the planet of 2045. Behind the game, the same pipeline powers a screening console for engineers, investors and local authorities, with provenance labels, transparent scoring and an executive PDF report. Our goal is to teach students, families and decision-makers to read Earth trends critically and to turn satellite data into earlier, better-informed action.
details:
WHAT WE BUILT

TERRA 2045 · The Last Journey is a 3D web game (Next.js, React, three.js) connected to a scientific backend (FastAPI). It is the front door to the Los Causas Espaciales platform.

THE STORY

In 2045 the Earth is lost and humanity lives in a lunar colony. The player activates the Genesis machine and travels back to 2026. On a 3D globe the player picks one of 57 real places grouped by continent (Moquegua, Lima, Taal, Etna, Mexico City, the Aral Sea, Tuvalu and more). The ship lands on the real terrain of the place, built from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 elevation and coloured with ESA WorldCover land cover. The player walks, talks to neighbours and reads the data.

HOW A PLACE IS WON (THE TREND-DETECTIVE LOOP)

1. Read the evidence: temperature and rainfall trends since 2001 from NASA POWER, tested with Mann-Kendall (Hamed-Rao correction) and Theil-Sen slope. "Not significant" is taught as "the evidence is not enough".

2. Check a second witness: each warming label says whether ERA5 confirms it (15 of 35 places with a trend). An atypical rainfall year is a "false clue" only where the reanalysis exceeds the satellite product (GPM IMERG / CHIRPS) at least five times (3 places). Example: in Moquegua, MERRA-2 reports a 300 mm extreme day in 2022, while IMERG reports 12 mm and CHIRPS 17 mm.

3. Decide with limited resources and warn the whole town before the event. The disaster events (mudslide, flood, heat, eruption, avalanche) are simulated: the team chose one per place from its known hazards, and the alert card says it is simulated.

Every place kept safe heals the planet of 2045, which the player sees when returning to the colony.

THE PLATFORM BEHIND THE GAME

The same typed data contract powers a screening console for infrastructure investors, engineers, environmental teams and public institutions: select a point, an official territory or a custom corridor; the pipeline retrieves Earth data, validates geometry and units, tests trends, compares independent sources and returns discoveries, limitations, a multicriteria score, financial scenarios and a downloadable executive PDF. Every value carries a provenance class (real, cached, model estimate, user assumption, illustrative, unavailable). A missing answer never means "no risk".

VALIDATION EXAMPLES

- Moquegua: 9 NASA POWER cells show significant warming, up to +0.42 °C per decade.

- Lurigancho-Chosica landslides: national and NASA susceptibility maps agree at 7 of 9 sample points.

- Marcona wind: NASA POWER 6.39 m/s vs Global Wind Atlas 9.74 m/s; operating wind-farm data (COES) support the atlas case, and NASA stays as the adverse scenario.

WHY IT MATTERS

Climate trends are invisible until disaster arrives. TERRA 2045 makes them visible and personal for schoolchildren, families and local authorities, and teaches the habit that matters most in Earth science: check the evidence, compare sources and act early. It is a learning and screening tool, not an early-warning service and not a substitute for engineering or local authorities.

HOW TO PLAY

Windows 10/11: download the repository as ZIP from GitHub, extract it, double-click PREPARAR.bat the first time and JUGAR.bat afterwards. The README explains every click.

TEAM

Christian Venegas Calderon, Nikol Estefany Borja Ugarte, Abel Andrés Valle Zuta, Mario Edgardo Alaluna Agüero. NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Moquegua local event, Peru.
